text:
Colorado arrives in Philadelphia as the team controlling the play. At five on five, COL has taken 55% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in its games, while PHI sits at 34%. The Flyers' goal difference of -19 trails their expected -13.8, and finishing (-8.5 goals against the chances) has cost them, so they are better than their record. Even so, the model projects 3.39 expected goals for COL tonight and 2.49 for PHI. Special teams add to the Flyers' problems: they take 4.4 penalties a game, while COL's power play generates 0.82 expected goals per game against a PHI penalty kill that allows 0.69.

In net, projected starters Mackenzie Blackwood (COL) and Dan Vladar (PHI) have both started slowly. Blackwood is at -1.82 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops compared with an average one facing the same shots) with a .891 save percentage, while Vladar is at -1.22 with a .889. Last season they were far apart from those marks: Blackwood at 8.01 over 39 games, Vladar at 12.74 over 52. Form favors Colorado too. The Avalanche are 3-1-1 over their last five and have out-chanced every opponent in that stretch, while the Flyers are 1-3-1 and won the chance battle in two of five.

Nathan MacKinnon gives COL a 45% chance to score and 88% to record a point, with Martin Necas at 35% and 76%. Nazem Kadri has no goals in eight games on 3.2 expected goals, and the model flags him as due. For PHI, Trevor Zegras (25% to score) leads the group, and Owen Tippett, now day-to-day, could return. Travis Konecny is out on injured reserve. Noah Juulsen also returns to Philadelphia for the first time since leaving the Flyers, a storyline the model doesn't price.
